mainTopic: When an offering slaughtered for the sake of another offering stays kosher (רבי אליעזר, שמעון אחי עזריה), and בן בתירא's view that the whole 14th is the time of the פסח
overview: The amud opens with רבי יהושע challenging רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר about offerings slaughtered for the sake of a פסח. רבי אליעזר answers that a פסח is special because it is kosher for its own sake only at its set time. The גמרא then turns to שמעון אחי עזריה, who says an offering slaughtered for the sake of a holier offering stays kosher, and it finds his source in the words ״אשר ירימו״. That same פסוק also teaches שמואל's law about eating טבל. רבי זירא asks whether, for שמעון אחי עזריה, such offerings also count for the owner. A proof from the בכור clause of the משנה is rejected, because that clause is needed to teach 'higher and lower' even among קדשים קלים. A new משנה follows. It brings the מחלוקת of רבי יהושע and בן בתירא about a פסח slaughtered שלא לשמו on the morning of the 14th, and בן עזאי's tradition from the seventy-two elders. The גמרא explains that for בן בתירא the whole 14th is the time of the פסח, because he reads 'בין הערבים' as 'between the two evenings.' It then tests this reading against the תמיד, the lamps of the מנורה and the קטרת, and the answer about the קטרת continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יהושע shows the same reasoning leads to a wrong result
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע builds a parallel קל וחומר using עולה and חטאת. It would make an עולה slaughtered for the sake of a חטאת פסול, which is not the הלכה. So reasoning of this kind cannot be trusted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: We find that leftover money of a sin offering is used for a burnt offering, but leftover money of a burnt offering is never used for a sin offering. So follow your logic. A sin offering, whose leftover can become a burnt offering, is still unfit if you slaughter it for the sake of a burnt offering. Then a burnt offering, whose leftover can never become a sin offering, should surely be unfit if you slaughter it for the sake of a sin offering! But that is not true.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע argues against רבי אליעזר. He builds an argument with the same pattern that leads to a conclusion everyone agrees is false.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two facts he starts from are true: a חטאת's leftover can go to an עולה, but not the reverse, and a חטאת slaughtered as an עולה is פסול. From these, the קל וחומר concludes that an עולה slaughtered as a חטאת should also be פסול. But the הלכה is that it is kosher. If this kind of reasoning gives a false result here, רבי אליעזר's similar reasoning about פסח is also suspect.

keyTerms.meaning: Leftover: money or an animal set aside for an offering that ended up not being needed
Burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
For the sake of: slaughtering with a specific offering in mind
Isn't it logical? The standard way of finishing a קל וחומר

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע does not actually hold that an עולה slaughtered for a חטאת is פסול. He builds this argument only to show that it leads to a wrong result, which proves the method is flawed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:
We find that a leftover sin offering is brought as a burnt offering,
but a leftover burnt offering is not brought as a sin offering.
Now, just as a sin offering, whose leftover is brought as a burnt offering,
if one slaughtered it for the sake of a burnt offering, it is unfit;
then a burnt offering, whose leftover is not brought as a sin offering,
if one slaughtered it for the sake of a sin offering,
isn't it logical that it should be unfit?!
phrases.notes: The punchline: this result is wrong, because an עולה slaughtered for a חטאת is kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי אליעזר's earlier argument that offerings slaughtered for the sake of a פסח are פסול.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's reasoning that other offerings slaughtered for the sake of a פסח become פסול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He shows the same kind of reasoning gives a false result: an עולה slaughtered for a חטאת would become פסול. So the reasoning is flawed.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר shows how a פסח differs from a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר rejects the comparison. A חטאת is kosher for its own sake all year, but a פסח only at its time. Since a פסח outside its time is itself פסול, other offerings slaughtered for its sake are also פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to him: No. You say a sin offering doesn't disqualify others slaughtered for its sake. That is because a sin offering is kosher for its own sake the whole year. Can you say the same about the Paschal offering, which is kosher for its own sake only at its set time? Since it is unfit for its own sake the rest of the year, it makes sense that other offerings are disqualified when slaughtered for its sake.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר defends his argument. He shows that the פסח has a special feature the חטאת does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת is always a valid offering for its own sake, so slaughtering another animal 'for the sake of a חטאת' does not ruin it. A פסח is valid for its own sake only on its day. Because the פסח itself is often פסול, its name has a weaker, disqualifying power, so other offerings slaughtered for its sake become פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: No; if you said: the opening of a reply that shows two cases are different
Paschal offering, brought on the afternoon of the 14th of ניסן

steps.whatToRemember: A חטאת is kosher for its own sake all year, while a פסח is kosher only at its time. According to רבי אליעזר, this is why slaughtering other offerings for the sake of a פסח makes them פסול.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to him: No;
if you said this about a sin offering,
phrases.notes: "This" means that other offerings slaughtered for a חטאת's sake stay kosher.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן כְּשֵׁרָה לִשְׁמָהּ כׇּל הַשָּׁנָה כּוּלָּהּ,
phrases.english: that is because it is fit for its own sake the entire year;
will you say the same about the Paschal offering,
which is fit for its own sake only at its time?!
Since it is unfit for its own sake,
phrases.notes: He means the rest of the year, outside its set time.

phrases.english: it is logical that other offerings are disqualified for its sake.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: לֹא; אִם אָמַרְתָּ בְּחַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהושע's challenge by showing that the חטאת and the פסח are not alike.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the two cases are different (פירכא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע assumed the פסח works just like the חטאת, so the reasoning must fail for both.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסח is unique because it is valid for its own sake only at its time. That makes other offerings slaughtered for its sake פסול.

steps.title: Moving on to שמעון אחי עזריה in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the start of the next opinion in the משנה, שמעון אחי עזריה, to begin discussing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמעון אחי עזריה says, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next topic. It quotes the opening words of שמעון אחי עזריה's opinion in the משנה so it can discuss it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line adds no new הלכה yet. It is a heading that points back to the משנה. In the משנה, שמעון אחי עזריה says an offering slaughtered for the sake of a higher-level offering stays kosher, and for the sake of a lower-level one becomes פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: שמעון, brother of עזריה: a תנא quoted in the משנה
Etc.: short for the rest of the quote

phrases.english: Shimon, brother of Azarya, says, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע discussion and opens a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It quotes שמעון אחי עזריה's opinion as the next subject to discuss.

steps.title: The פסוק behind שמעון אחי עזריה's view
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן (or רבי ינאי) derives the view of שמעון אחי עזריה from the פסוק ״ולא יחללו את קדשי בני ישראל את אשר ירימו לה׳״. An offering is not ruined by being slaughtered for the sake of a holier offering. It is only ruined by being slaughtered for the sake of a less holy one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי teaches in the name of רבי יוחנן, and רב אחא son of רבא teaches in the name of רבי ינאי: What is the reason of שמעון אחי עזריה? The verse says: 'And they shall not profane the holy things of the children of Israel, which they will raise up to ה׳.' They are not profaned by what is raised above them. They are profaned by what is lower than them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the source for the view of שמעון אחי עזריה, which it quoted in the previous step. Two teachers pass on the same explanation, each in the name of a different earlier sage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״ירימו״ comes from the root meaning 'raise up.' So the פסוק is read as a rule about holiness levels. Slaughtering for the sake of something 'higher' does not profane the offering, but slaughtering for the sake of something 'lower' does.

keyTerms.meaning: they will raise up / set apart

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָשֵׁי מַתְנֵי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: Rav Ashi teaches in the name of Rabbi Yochanan,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא מַתְנֵי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: and Rav Acha son of Rava teaches it in the name of Rabbi Yannai:
What is the reason of Shimon brother of Azarya?
Because the verse says:
'And they shall not profane the holy things of the children of Israel
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:15

phrases.english: which they will raise up to ה׳'
by what is raised higher than them, they are not profaned,
phrases.notes: He reads ״ירימו״ as 'raised up,' meaning a holier offering. Slaughtering for its sake leaves the offering kosher.

phrases.english: by what is lower than them, they are profaned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the opinion that Step 3 introduced.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offerings are not disqualified when slaughtered for the sake of holier offerings. They are disqualified only when slaughtered for the sake of less holy ones. This is derived from ״אשר ירימו״.

steps.title: The verse is already needed for שמואל's law about untithed produce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that this same פסוק is needed by שמואל. He uses it to teach that someone who eats טבל is liable to מיתה בידי שמים, reading ״אשר ירימו״ as 'which they will set apart in the future.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this verse really come for that? It is needed for שמואל's teaching. שמואל said: From where do we know that one who eats untithed produce is liable to death? Because it says, 'And they shall not profane the holy things of the children of Israel which they will set apart to ה׳.' The verse speaks of things that are going to be set apart in the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the derivation from the last step. It points out that שמואל already uses this same פסוק for a completely different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל reads ״ירימו״ as future tense: produce whose תרומה has not yet been separated, which is טבל. The פסוק then warns against 'profaning' it by eating it. If the פסוק is used for that, how can it also teach the rule of שמעון אחי עזריה?

keyTerms.meaning: does this verse come for this purpose?
produce from which תרומה and מעשרות have not yet been separated
death, here at the hands of Heaven
things that are going to be set apart as תרומה

phrases.english: And does this verse come for that?!
But it is needed for Shmuel's teaching!
For Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לָאוֹכֵל אֶת הַטֶּבֶל שֶׁהוּא בְּמִיתָה?
phrases.english: From where do we know that one who eats untithed produce is liable to death?
phrases.notes: This means death at the hands of Heaven, not a punishment carried out by a בית דין.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְלֹא יְחַלְּלוּ אֶת קׇדְשֵׁי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: As it says: 'And they shall not profane the holy things of the children of Israel
which they will set apart to ה׳'
the verse speaks of things that are going to be set apart in the future.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 4's use of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation of שמעון אחי עזריה's rule from ״אשר ירימו״.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is already used by שמואל for the law of eating טבל, so it should not be free to teach another law.

steps.title: The unusual wording teaches both laws
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that if only one law were meant, the תורה could have written ״אשר הורמו״ ('which were set apart'). The choice of ״אשר ירימו״ shows that the פסוק teaches two laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the verse write 'which were set apart.' Why does it say 'which they will set apart'? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection by pointing to the special wording of the פסוק. It concludes that the פסוק teaches both the rule of שמעון אחי עזריה and the law of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain past form ״הורמו״ would have been enough to talk about holy things in general. The form ״ירימו״ does double work: its future tense hints at טבל, and its root 'raise up' hints at holiness levels. So nothing is wasted, and both laws are learned.
steps.whatToRemember: One פסוק, ״אשר ירימו״, teaches two laws. Offerings slaughtered for a holier offering stay kosher (שמעון אחי עזריה), and eating טבל is punished with מיתה (שמואל).

phrases.english: If so, let the verse write 'which were set apart';
Why does it say 'which they will set apart'?
Learn two things from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the objection of Step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra or unusual wording in the פסוק allows two derivations.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק can only serve one purpose, so it cannot teach both laws.
steps.terutzMaskana: The unusual form ״ירימו״ teaches both שמואל's law about טבל and the rule of שמעון אחי עזריה.

steps.title: רבי זירא asks how far שמעון אחי עזריה disagrees
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks about the case where שמעון אחי עזריה says the offering is kosher. Is it kosher but does not count for the owner, as the חכמים hold? Then he disagrees with them on only one point. Or is it kosher and also counts for the owner? Then they disagree on two points.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא asked: Are they kosher but do not count for the owner? Then when he disagrees, he disagrees on one point. Or perhaps they are kosher and do count, and they disagree on two points?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא asks a question to clarify the view of שמעון אחי עזריה. The question is about the offerings that he says remain kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים of the משנה hold that offerings slaughtered for a different purpose are kosher but do not fulfill the owner's obligation. If שמעון אחי עזריה agrees about that, his only disagreement is that he makes the 'lower' cases fully פסול. If he holds the 'higher' cases even count for the owner, he disagrees with the חכמים on that point too.

keyTerms.meaning: bring atonement, meaning they count for the owner's obligation

steps.confusionAlert: Kosher is not the same as counting for the owner. In this sugya an offering can be valid and still fail to fulfill the owner's obligation, so he must bring another one.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira asked:
Are they kosher but do not count for the owner?
phrases.notes: He means the offerings slaughtered for the sake of a holier offering, the ones שמעון אחי עזריה calls kosher.

phrases.english: Then when he disagrees, he disagrees on one point,
or perhaps they are kosher and do count for the owner,
and they disagree on two points?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the source is settled, opens a new question about the exact scope of the view of שמעון אחי עזריה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to שמעון אחי עזריה, do offerings slaughtered for a holier offering also fulfill the owner's obligation, or are they only kosher?

steps.title: אביי brings a teaching about a firstborn and a tithe animal
steps.stepSummary: אביי (or רבי זריקא) quotes the end of שמעון אחי עזריה's own words in our משנה: a בכור or מעשר slaughtered for the sake of שלמים is kosher, but שלמים slaughtered for the sake of a בכור or מעשר are פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי (some say רבי זריקא) said: Come and hear. A firstborn or a tithe animal slaughtered for the sake of a peace offering is kosher. A peace offering slaughtered for the sake of a firstborn or a tithe animal is not kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is setting up an answer to רבי זירא's question by quoting a source. Here he only quotes it; in the next step he will draw the proof from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This clause of the משנה applies שמעון אחי עזריה's rule: going up to a holier offering is fine, and going down to a less holy one ruins it. שלמים count as holier than a בכור or מעשר. The proof is not stated yet; it depends on what 'kosher' means for a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn animal, given to a כהן and brought as an offering
The tithe animal, every tenth animal, brought as an offering

phrases.english: Abaye said, and some say it was Rabbi Zerika:
Come and hear:
The firstborn and the tithe animal
that one slaughtered for the sake of peace offerings are kosher.
Peace offerings that one slaughtered for the sake of a firstborn
or for the sake of a tithe animal are not kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי זְרִיקָא, תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins an attempt to answer רבי זירא's question from step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That according to שמעון אחי עזריה, an offering slaughtered for a holier offering is kosher but does not count for the owner.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of שמעון אחי עזריה's statement in the משנה, about a בכור and מעשר slaughtered for the sake of שלמים.

steps.title: A firstborn never brings atonement, so the earlier clause works the same way
steps.stepSummary: A בכור does not bring atonement, so 'kosher' in its case must mean kosher without counting. Since that is the meaning in the later clause, the earlier clause must mean the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think 'kosher' means kosher and it also counts, can a firstborn bring atonement at all? So it must mean kosher but it does not count. And since the later clause means kosher but not counting, the earlier clause also means kosher but not counting.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי now draws his proof. In the משנה, 'kosher' for a בכור can only mean that it does not count, so the same must be true throughout שמעון אחי עזריה's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור is not brought to gain atonement, so 'counting for the owner' cannot even apply to it. That forces 'kosher' in the סיפא to mean kosher without counting. אביי assumes the רישא, about lighter offerings slaughtered for the sake of most-holy ones, uses 'kosher' the same way. That would answer רבי זירא's question: שמעון disagrees with the חכמים on only one point.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it enters your mind: introduces a possibility that is about to be rejected
They bring atonement, meaning the offering counts for the owner
The later clause of a teaching
The earlier clause of a teaching

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse 'kosher' (כשר) with 'counts for the owner' (מרצה). An offering can be kosher on the מזבח and still not fulfill the owner's obligation. That gap is the whole question here.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that they are kosher and also count for the owner,
is a firstborn something that brings atonement?!
Rather, they are kosher but do not count!
And since the later clause means kosher but not counting,
the earlier clause also means kosher but not counting!
phrases.notes: The 'earlier clause' is the start of this same teaching, about lighter offerings slaughtered for most-holy ones, quoted at the end of step 11.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the proof from the clause of the משנה quoted in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That שמעון אחי עזריה holds 'kosher but does not count,' like the חכמים, and disagrees on only one point.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact that a בכור never brings atonement, plus the assumption that the רישא and סיפא of one teaching match.

steps.title: Each clause may follow its own rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the two clauses are not comparable. Each can stay as it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are these cases comparable?! This one is as it is, and that one is as it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down אביי's proof. The earlier clause and the later clause do not have to mean the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the סיפא, the בכור does not count only because a בכור can never count. In the רישא, the lighter offering might really count for its owner. So we cannot learn the רישא from the סיפא, and רבי זירא's question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Are they comparable?: used to reject a comparison between two cases
This is as it is, and that is as it is: each case keeps its own rule

phrases.english: Are the cases comparable?!
This one is as it is,
and that one is as it is.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִידֵּי אִירְיָא? הָא כִּדְאִיתַהּ, וְהָא כִּדְאִיתַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference made in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the step from the סיפא to the רישא, not the reading of the סיפא itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The בכור case does not count for a special reason, because a בכור never brings atonement, so it cannot teach about other offerings.

steps.title: Then why is the second clause needed at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rejection: if the בכור clause does not teach 'kosher but not counting,' what does it add? 'Higher and lower' was already taught in the earlier clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what is it teaching us? Is it teaching us about higher and lower holiness? We already learned that: How so? Most-holy offerings slaughtered for the sake of lighter offerings, and so on!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the rejection in step 10. If the בכור clause teaches nothing new, it seems pointless, because the earlier clause already showed the 'higher and lower' rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A teaching is not supposed to repeat itself for no reason. If the סיפא only repeats that going up is fine and going down is not, it adds nothing to the רישא. So the סיפא must be there to teach something new, likely 'kosher but not counting.' That brings back אביי's proof.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us?: asks what new point a teaching adds
Higher and lower: offerings of greater and lesser holiness

steps.whyThisMatters: This uses the rule that a teaching should not repeat itself without reason, to bring back the proof that was just rejected.

phrases.english: Rather, what is it teaching us?
phrases.notes: 'It' is the later clause, about the בכור and מעשר.

phrases.english: Is it teaching us about higher and lower holiness?!
We already learned it:
How so? Most-holy offerings
that one slaughtered for the sake of lighter offerings, and so on!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 10 by arguing that it would leave the סיפא repeating the רישא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rejection in step 10, which says the בכור clause need not mean 'kosher but not counting' for other offerings.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the סיפא only teaches that higher and lower holiness matter, it repeats the רישא, so it must be teaching something new.

steps.title: The בכור clause teaches 'higher and lower' even among lighter offerings
steps.stepSummary: The בכור clause is needed so we do not think 'higher and lower' only applies between קדשי קדשים and קדשים קלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought that 'higher and lower' only exists between קדשי קדשים and קדשים קלים, but not between two kinds of קדשים קלים. So the בכור clause teaches that it does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 11, which asked what the בכור clause adds. It says the clause teaches something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier clause showed 'higher and lower' between very holy and less holy offerings. בכור, מעשר and שלמים are all קדשים קלים, so one might think they count as equal. The בכור clause shows that even within קדשים קלים one offering can be 'higher' than another.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said / lest you think

steps.confusionAlert: This answer saves the דחיה of step 10. The בכור clause does not have to mean 'kosher but not counting,' because it already teaches something else.

phrases.english: Lest you say:
offerings of the highest holiness and offerings of lighter holiness
that is where there is 'higher and lower,'
but lighter and lighter, no.
phrases.notes: He means two offerings that are both קדשים קלים, like בכור and שלמים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11 by showing what the בכור clause adds.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the clause teaches a new point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Higher and lower' only exists between קדשי קדשים and קדשים קלים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even among קדשים קלים, one offering can be higher than another.

steps.title: Another משנה already teaches that שלמים outrank בכור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that this point is already taught in a משנה about which offering comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: We already learned this: שלמים come before the בכור, because they need blood placed on four sides, leaning of hands, libations, and waving of the breast and thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 12. It says another משנה already shows that שלמים are 'higher' than a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a different משנה already ranks שלמים above בכור, then our משנה would not need to teach it. So the answer of step 12 seems to fail, and the question of step 11 returns.

keyTerms.meaning: This too we have already learned
Placing the blood so it reaches the four sides of the מזבח
Waving of the breast and thigh

phrases.english: This too we have already learned:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה later in זבחים (89a) about which offering is brought first.

phrases.english: Peace offerings come before the firstborn,
because they require the blood to be placed on four sides,
and leaning of hands, and libations,
and waving of the breast and thigh!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 12 as already known from elsewhere.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the בכור clause is needed to teach 'higher and lower' among קדשים קלים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה already ranks שלמים above בכור, so the clause adds nothing.

steps.title: Our משנה is the main source; the other one mentions it in passing
steps.stepSummary: The rule is taught mainly here. The other משנה only brings it up along the way.
steps.simpleTranslation: This משנה is the main place for this rule. That other משנה just mentions it in passing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of step 13 by saying which משנה is the real source of the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having the rule in two places is not a problem if one is the main teaching. The other משנה is about the order of offerings and only uses the ranking along the way. So the בכור clause here is still needed, and the דחיה of step 10 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It brought it along in passing

steps.whatToRemember: The proof of steps 8-9 is rejected. The בכור clause teaches 'higher and lower' among קדשים קלים, so we still cannot tell what שמעון אחי עזריה means by 'kosher.'

phrases.english: This one is the main place,
that one brings it in passing.
phrases.notes: Literally 'it took it along by dragging,' meaning it was mentioned while teaching something else.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13 and closes this discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Main source versus mention in passing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two משניות teach the same rule, so one is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה is the main source; the other only uses the rule along the way.

steps.title: A פסח slaughtered not for its sake on the morning of the 14th
steps.stepSummary: New משנה: רבי יהושע says it is kosher, like the 13th. בן בתירא says it is פסול, like the afternoon of the 14th.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone slaughtered a פסח on the morning of the 14th of ניסן, not for the sake of a פסח: רבי יהושע says it is kosher, as if it were slaughtered on the 13th. בן בתירא says it is פסול, as if it were slaughtered in the afternoon.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It brings a מחלוקת about a פסח slaughtered שלא לשמו on the morning of the 14th, before its proper time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה compares this case to two others. Slaughtered on the 13th, it is kosher; slaughtered in the afternoon of the 14th, its proper time, it is פסול. רבי יהושע treats the morning like the 13th. בן בתירא treats it like the afternoon.

keyTerms.meaning: Not for its own sake (for a different offering)
The afternoon, the proper time for the פסח

steps.whyThisMatters: The question is whether the morning of the 14th already counts as the פסח's own time. The rest of the sugya builds on this.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The Pesach offering that one slaughtered
in the morning on the fourteenth
not for its sake:
Rabbi Yehoshua deems it fit,
as though it were slaughtered on the thirteenth.
Ben Beteira deems it unfit,
as though it were slaughtered in the afternoon.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַפֶּסַח שֶׁשְּׁחָטוֹ שַׁחֲרִית בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע: kosher, like the 13th. בן בתירא: פסול, like the afternoon of the 14th.

steps.title: בן עזאי's tradition from the seventy-two elders
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי reports a tradition: eaten offerings slaughtered not for their sake are kosher but do not count for the owner, except the פסח and the חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמעון בן עזאי said: I received a tradition from seventy-two elders, on the day they seated רבי אליעזר at the head of the ישיבה, that all offerings that are eaten and were slaughtered not for their sake are kosher, but they do not count for the owner's obligation. The exceptions are the פסח and the חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a new voice, שמעון בן עזאי, who reports a tradition he received from a large gathering of elders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tradition is limited to offerings that are eaten. For these, slaughtering not for their sake leaves the animal kosher, but the owner must still bring another offering. The פסח and the חטאת are exceptions: for them, the wrong intent makes the offering פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: not for their own sake, with the wrong offering in mind
did not count for the owner's obligation

phrases.english: Shimon ben Azzai said:
I have received a tradition from the mouth of
seventy-two elders

phrases.aramaic: בַּיּוֹם שֶׁהוֹשִׁיבוּ אֶת רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בִּישִׁיבָה,
phrases.english: on the day they seated Rabbi Eliezer in the yeshiva,
phrases.notes: The words say אליעזר, but this is the famous day רבי אלעזר בן עזריה was appointed head of the ישיבה.

phrases.english: that all the offerings that are eaten
that were slaughtered not for their sake are kosher,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא עָלוּ לַבְּעָלִים מִשּׁוּם חוֹבָה;
phrases.english: except that they did not count for the owners as their obligation;
except for the Paschal offering and the sin offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן עַזַּאי: מְקוּבָּל אֲנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה after the argument between רבי יהושע and בן בתירא, adding בן עזאי's tradition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eaten offerings slaughtered not for their sake are kosher but do not count for the owner, except the פסח and the חטאת, which become פסול.

steps.title: בן עזאי added only the עולה, and the חכמים disagreed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה concludes that בן עזאי's only addition to the list of exceptions was the עולה, and the חכמים rejected it.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן עזאי added nothing except the burnt offering, and the חכמים did not agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sums up what is new in בן עזאי's view and tells us the חכמים did not accept it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His tradition spoke only about offerings that are eaten. So the only change from the standard rule is that he also counts the עולה, which is not eaten, as פסול when slaughtered not for its sake. The חכמים say the עולה is kosher, just like other offerings, and only the פסח and חטאת are exceptions.

keyTerms.meaning: burnt offering, completely burned on the מזבח and not eaten
the Sages did not agree with him

steps.whatToRemember: The standard rule lists two exceptions, פסח and חטאת. בן עזאי adds the עולה as a third, and the חכמים reject that addition.

phrases.english: And ben Azzai did not add anything
phrases.notes: He means: added to the two exceptions already listed, פסח and חטאת.

phrases.english: except the burnt offering,
and the Sages did not agree with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא הוֹסִיף בֶּן עַזַּאי אֶלָּא הָעוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the bottom line from בן עזאי's tradition in step 16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: בן עזאי's only addition is the עולה, and the חכמים rule against him.

steps.title: בן בתירא holds that the whole fourteenth is the time of the פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר quotes רבי אושעיא: בן בתירא would declare kosher a פסח slaughtered for its own sake on the morning of the fourteenth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי אושעיא: בן בתירא would declare kosher a פסח slaughtered on the morning of the fourteenth for its own sake, because the whole day is its time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and draws a new point from בן בתירא's opinion in the משנה (step 15).
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, בן בתירא said a morning פסח slaughtered not for its sake is פסול, just like one in the afternoon. That means he treats the morning as already the פסח's proper time. So if it was slaughtered for its own sake, it should be fully kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: for its own sake, with the right intent
since the whole day is its time

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that בן בתירא's view has a positive side: the morning is fully valid for the פסח, not just a time when the wrong intent ruins it.

phrases.english: GEMARA:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Oshaya said:
Ben Beteira would declare kosher
a Paschal offering that one slaughtered in the morning
on the fourteenth, for its own sake,
since the whole day is its time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא: מַכְשִׁיר הָיָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא by drawing a ruling out of בן בתירא's position in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בן בתירא, a פסח slaughtered for its own sake on the morning of the fourteenth is kosher, because the whole day is its time.

steps.title: Why did the משנה say 'as though'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the morning is truly the פסח's time, why does בן בתירא say it is only 'as though' it were slaughtered in the afternoon?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the meaning of 'as though'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אושעיא's reading using the exact wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'as though it were the afternoon' sounds like the morning is not really the afternoon, only treated like it. That suggests a difference between morning and afternoon, which goes against the claim that the whole day is equally the time of the פסח.

phrases.english: And what is "as though"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 18 based on the wording of בן בתירא's statement in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אושעיא's claim that, for בן בתירא, the whole day is fully the time of the פסח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'as though' implies the morning is only compared to the afternoon, not the same as it.

steps.title: בן בתירא just copied רבי יהושע's wording
steps.stepSummary: The word 'as though' is only a matter of style: since רבי יהושע said 'as though,' בן בתירא answered with the same word.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since רבי יהושע said 'as though,' בן בתירא also said 'as though.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word 'as though' teaches nothing about the law. בן בתירא was simply matching the wording of the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע said 'as though it were slaughtered on the 13th.' בן בתירא replied in the same style, 'as though in the afternoon.' In his real view, morning and afternoon of the fourteenth are exactly the same, so רבי אושעיא's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: since, because (one side said it, the other matched the wording)

steps.whatToRemember: For בן בתירא, the whole fourteenth is the time of the פסח. A morning פסח for its own sake is kosher. The word 'as though' is only a matching style of speech.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'as though' as a real legal difference between morning and afternoon. The גמרא says it is only borrowed wording.

phrases.english: Since Rabbi Yehoshua said "as though,"
he too said "as though."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 19 and defends רבי אושעיא's reading from step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic explanation: the wording follows the other opinion's phrasing and carries no legal meaning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'As though' means the morning is only treated like the afternoon and is not truly the פסח's time.
steps.terutzMaskana: בן בתירא only copied רבי יהושע's phrasing. For him, the whole day really is the פסח's time.

steps.title: Why not present the argument about a פסח slaughtered for its own sake?
steps.stepSummary: If בן בתירא really holds the morning is the פסח's time, the משנה should have shown the argument in the clearer case of לשמו.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then instead of arguing about a פסח slaughtered not for its sake, let them argue about one slaughtered for its sake!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges how the משנה chose to present the argument between רבי יהושע and בן בתירא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אושעיא, בן בתירא says a פסח slaughtered לשמו in the morning is kosher, while רבי יהושע would say it is פסול. That is a clear and sharp argument. So why did the משנה present the argument in the case of שלא לשמו instead?

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if what was just said is true)
About an animal slaughtered for its own sake (as a פסח)

phrases.english: If so,
rather than arguing about one slaughtered not for its sake,
let them argue about one slaughtered for its sake!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אַדְּמִיפַּלְגִי בְּשֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ – לִיפַּלְגוּ בְּלִשְׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that the morning is truly the פסח's time for בן בתירא and questions the way the משנה framed the argument.
steps.kashyaTarget: The way the משנה presents the argument (שלא לשמו instead of לשמו)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the clearest difference between them is in the לשמו case, the משנה should have shown the argument there.

steps.title: The שלא לשמו case teaches something new
steps.stepSummary: Had the משנה shown only the לשמו case, we would think רבי יהושע agrees in the שלא לשמו case, because part of the day is fit for the פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they had argued only about one slaughtered for its sake, I would have said that in a case of not for its sake, רבי יהושע agrees with בן בתירא, since part of the day is fit. So the משנה teaches us that they argue there too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה chose the שלא לשמו case: it teaches that רבי יהושע disagrees even there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the שלא לשמו case, one might think רבי יהושע would also call it פסול, because the afternoon of that same day is fit for the פסח. By putting the argument in this case, the משנה shows that רבי יהושע still treats the morning like the thirteenth, so the animal is kosher, as a different offering.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first assumption)
Since part of it (the day) is fit
It teaches us (that this assumption is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה put the argument in the שלא לשמו case to show that רבי יהושע disagrees even there, even though the afternoon of that same day is fit for the פסח.

phrases.english: If they had argued about one slaughtered for its sake,
I would have said:
but in a case of not for its sake,
רבי יהושע agrees with בן בתירא,
since part of it is fit;
phrases.notes: "Part of it" means part of the day: the afternoon is the proper time for the פסח.

phrases.english: so it teaches us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a new point (חידוש) that the chosen case teaches
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In the שלא לשמו case רבי יהושע would agree it is פסול, since the afternoon of that day is fit.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even in the שלא לשמו case, רבי יהושע disagrees and calls it kosher.

steps.title: But the פסוק says 'בין הערבים'
steps.stepSummary: How can בן בתירא allow a פסח in the morning, when the תורה says to slaughter it 'בין הערבים' (in the afternoon)?
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written: 'בין הערבים'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges בן בתירא's view from a פסוק that seems to require the פסח to be slaughtered in the afternoon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The simple meaning of 'בין הערבים' is the afternoon. If so, the morning should not be a valid time for the פסח, which goes against בן בתירא as רבי אושעיא explained him.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? (a challenge from a פסוק)

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"in the afternoon"!
phrases.notes: שמות 12:6

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from how the משנה is worded to a challenge from a פסוק against בן בתירא's position.
steps.kashyaTarget: בן בתירא's view that the morning of the fourteenth is a valid time for the פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק requires 'בין הערבים', which seems to mean only the afternoon.

steps.title: 'Between the two evenings' means the whole day
steps.stepSummary: עולא בריה דרב עילאי explains that בן בתירא reads 'בין הערבים' as 'between the two evenings', which includes the whole day.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא, son of רב עילאי, said: it means between two evenings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by showing that בן בתירא reads the פסוק differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בן בתירא, 'בין הערבים' does not mean 'afternoon'. It means the time between the evening that starts the fourteenth and the evening that ends it. That covers the whole day, so the morning is valid too.

keyTerms.meaning: Between two evenings, meaning the whole day between them

steps.whatToRemember: בן בתירא reads 'בין הערבים' as 'between the two evenings', so the whole fourteenth day, including the morning, is the time of the פסח.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two readings: the usual reading is 'afternoon', but בן בתירא reads it as the whole day.

phrases.english: Ulla, son of Rav Ilai, said:
Between two evenings.
phrases.notes: The evening when the fourteenth begins and the evening when it ends, so the whole day counts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב עִילַּאי: בֵּין שְׁנֵי עֲרָבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the פסוק in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the פסוק a different way
steps.terutzMaskana: For בן בתירא, 'בין הערבים' means between the two evenings, which is the whole day.

steps.title: Would the daily offering also be fit all day?
steps.stepSummary: If 'בין הערבים' means the whole day, then the afternoon תמיד, which uses the same words, should also be fit all day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תמיד, about which it is written 'בין הערבים': is it also fit the whole day?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges עולא's reading of 'בין הערבים' by applying it to another offering that uses the same phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא said that 'between the two evenings' covers the whole day. The afternoon תמיד uses the exact same words. That would make the afternoon תמיד fit all day, which is clearly not the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily communal offering: one lamb in the morning and one in the afternoon
So too / would you also say

phrases.english: The daily offering, about which it is written:
phrases.notes: במדבר 28:4

phrases.english: "Bein ha'arbayim"
would you also say the whole day is fit?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation given in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's reading that 'בין הערבים' means the whole day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same words appear for the תמיד. Applying the reading there gives a result that cannot be right.

steps.title: The morning lamb shows the other lamb is in the afternoon
steps.stepSummary: For the תמיד, the פסוק says one lamb is brought in the morning, so 'בין הערבים' there must mean the actual afternoon.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, since it is written 'the one lamb you shall offer in the morning,' we learn that 'בין הערבים' means the real afternoon.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תמיד is different, because its פסוק sets the two lambs against each other: morning and 'בין הערבים'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the פסח there is no contrast, so 'בין הערבים' can mean the whole day. By the תמיד, the first lamb is tied to the morning. That contrast shows the second lamb belongs to the true afternoon.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in the case of the תמיד)
By inference, from this we learn

phrases.english: There, since it is written:
"The one lamb you shall offer in the morning",
we can infer that "bein ha'arbayim"
means the actual afternoon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases from the context of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בין הערבים' should mean the whole day everywhere, including by the תמיד.
steps.terutzMaskana: By the תמיד, the contrast with 'in the morning' limits 'בין הערבים' to the real afternoon.

steps.title: Maybe the second lamb can be brought any time
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the פסוק only means one lamb must be in the morning, while the other may be brought at any time of day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that one lamb is in the morning, and the other can be brought all day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. The morning lamb does not prove the second lamb must wait for the afternoon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'one lamb in the morning' could simply fix the first lamb. The second lamb, called 'בין הערבים', could still follow בן בתירא's reading and be fit all day, including the morning.

phrases.english: Say that one is in the morning,
and the other one all day!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference drawn in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that the morning lamb forces the second lamb into the afternoon
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק fixes only the first lamb. Nothing yet stops the second lamb from being brought at any time.

steps.title: 'One' in the morning means not two
steps.stepSummary: The word 'one' teaches that only one lamb may be brought in the morning. So the second lamb must be brought in the afternoon.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One in the morning' means: not two in the morning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by focusing on the word 'אחד'. The תורה limits the morning to only one lamb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'one' is not extra. It excludes bringing both lambs in the morning. So the second lamb cannot be brought in the morning, and its 'בין הערבים' must mean the real afternoon. This saves the difference between the תמיד and בן בתירא's reading of the פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: One, which here also means 'only one'

steps.whatToRemember: בן בתירא reads 'בין הערבים' as the whole day. By the תמיד it means the real afternoon, because the תורה says only 'one' lamb may be brought in the morning.

phrases.english: "One... in the morning"
and not two in the morning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27 and completes the defense of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exact reading of a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second lamb could be brought any time, even in the morning.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אחד' excludes a second morning lamb, so the second lamb must be in the actual afternoon.

steps.title: Can the lamps also be lit all day?
steps.stepSummary: The lamps of the מנורה are also described with 'בין הערבים'. Should they then be fit to light all day?
steps.simpleTranslation: The lamps of the מנורה are also described with the words 'בין הערבים'. So should we say that the whole day is fit for lighting them too?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another challenge to בן בתירא's reading. The lighting of the lamps uses the same words, 'בין הערבים'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 said 'בין הערבים' can mean the whole day. Step 28 explained why the afternoon תמיד is different. Now the גמרא points to a second case that uses the same words: lighting the מנורה. If the words mean 'all day', the lamps should be lit at any time of day, which sounds wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Usually 'in the afternoon'. בן בתירא reads it as 'between the two evenings', meaning the whole day

phrases.english: The lamps, where it is written 'bein ha'arbayim'
phrases.notes: שמות 30:8

phrases.english: so too, is the whole day fit?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the תמיד was explained, the גמרא tests the same reading against a second case that uses the same words.
steps.kashyaTarget: בן בתירא's reading that 'בין הערבים' means the whole day (step 24)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same words appear for lighting the lamps. If they mean 'all day', the lamps could be lit at any time of day, which is not the accepted practice.

steps.title: The lamps must burn from evening until morning
steps.stepSummary: The lamps are different because the תורה says they burn 'from evening until morning'. A ברייתא explains this phrase in two ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is different, because it is written: 'from evening until morning'. A ברייתא teaches about these words: Give the lamp enough oil so that it keeps burning from evening until morning. Another explanation: no service in the מקדש is valid from evening until morning except this one alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the lamps are a special case, because another פסוק ties them to evening and night. It brings a ברייתא with two explanations of that פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'from evening until morning' show that the lamps belong to the night. They are lit toward evening, not at any hour of the day. The first explanation says to put in enough oil to last all night. The second says this is the only service that is done at night. Either way, the meaning of 'בין הערבים' for the lamps is fixed by this second פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Its measure, the right amount of oil

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא gives two different explanations of the same words. Both lead to the same result here: the lamps belong to evening and night, so they are not lit at any time of day.

phrases.english: There it is different, because it is written:
'from evening until morning'
phrases.notes: שמות 27:21

phrases.english: And it is taught in a ברייתא: 'from evening until morning' means:
give it its measure
phrases.notes: He means give the lamp enough oil.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁתְּהֵא דּוֹלֶקֶת וְהוֹלֶכֶת מֵעֶרֶב וְעַד בֹּקֶר.
phrases.english: so that it keeps burning from evening until morning.
Another explanation:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לְךָ עֲבוֹדָה כְּשֵׁרָה מֵעֶרֶב וְעַד בֹּקֶר,
phrases.english: there is no service that is valid from evening until morning,
except this one alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the lamps.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case by pointing to a separate פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lamps, like any 'בין הערבים' service, could be lit all day.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'From evening until morning' ties the lamps to night, so they are lit toward evening.

steps.title: Can the incense also be burned all day?
steps.stepSummary: The קטרת is also described with 'בין הערבים'. Should it then be fit to burn all day?
steps.simpleTranslation: The קטרת is also described with the words 'בין הערבים'. So should we say that the whole day is fit for burning it too?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the same challenge again, this time about the קטרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק (שמות 30:8) that speaks about lighting the lamps also says to burn the קטרת 'בין הערבים'. The 'evening until morning' answer was about the lamps, so the גמרא asks how we know the קטרת is not burned at any hour of the day.

keyTerms.meaning: The incense burned in the מקדש
Where it is written about it

phrases.english: The incense, where it is written about it: 'bein ha'arbayim'
phrases.notes: שמות 30:8

phrases.english: so too, is the whole day fit?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 29, now applied to the קטרת.
steps.kashyaTarget: בן בתירא's reading that 'בין הערבים' means the whole day (step 24)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The קטרת uses the same words. The 'evening until morning' answer only covered the lamps, so the קטרת might seem fit all day.

steps.title: The incense is a different case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer: the קטרת is different. The reason comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: The incense is different,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer the question about the קטרת. This line only opens the answer, and the reason comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as it did with the lamps, the גמרא is going to show that the קטרת has its own reason why it cannot be done all day. For now it only says that the קטרת is a special case.

phrases.english: The incense is different,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the challenge from the קטרת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (the reason continues in the next lines)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קטרת, described with 'בין הערבים', could be burned all day.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קטרת is a special case, with the explanation still to come.
